description.en: COCONUT[KG] is a knowledge graph based on the Coconut Dataset, which is a comprehensive platform that facilitates natural product research by providing data, tools, and other resources and provides services for the deposition, curation, and reuse of data.

comment.en: Descriptive information related to synonyms, comments, or other textual metadata of a molecule.
The chemical and biological properties of a molecule.
Attributes related to the classification molecules.
A group of atoms bonded together, representing the smallest fundamental unit of a chemical compound that can take part in a chemical reaction.
Constitutional descriptors of a chemical compound.
Unique Identifiers for a given molecule.
Geometrical descriptors of a chemical compound.
A living thing that has an organized structure. The biological origin of a given molecule.
A geographical location where an organism is reported to be found.
Sample location within the organism from where the sample of the compound is taken.
An article, book or document with a DOI in which a molecule or a collection was mentioned.
Electronic descriptors of a chemical compound.
Descriptors of a molecule.
Groups of molecules are organized within collections, each linked to metadata such as titles, descriptions, and related jobs.
Attributes counting variants, collections, and other related data of a molecule.
Current state and activity of a molecule.
Indicates whether the molecule is a placeholder in the dataset, serving as a temporary or default entry without full attributes.
Number of Hydrogen Bond Acceptors in a molecule using the Lipinski module.
Indicates whether the collection is publicly accessible or private.
The molecular formula is a string that represents the types and number of atoms in the molecule.
The total number of synonyms associated with the molecule.
The slug of the sample location name.
The IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) is the internationalised version of the URI (Uniform Resource Identifier)
The molecule origintes from a certain organism.
A molecule is found in a geo location.
The sample location specifies the location of the organism it originated from.
The count of geographical occurrences or representations related to the molecule.
Molecule parent classification, allowing for traceability in hierarchical relationships.
Observations or notes about the structural characteristics of the molecule.
A collection is represented in an entry.
The formal charge of the molecule.
A SMILES representation of the molecule that excludes sugars.
The Standard International Chemical Identifier (InChI) for the molecule, providing a unique textual representation of its structure.
The Digital Object Identifier (DOI) assigned to the collection.
The parts of the organism from which molecules can be extracted.
A molecule has certain amounts of different countable properties.
A molecule is descriped by its properties.
The title of the collection.
The number of Hydrogen Bond Donors in a molecule.
The description of a given Collection.
A list of alternative names or terms that refer to the same molecule.
The current status of any processing or tasks associated with the collection.
Chemical Super Class generated using ClassyFire.
A unique identifier assigned to the molecule.
Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA) of a molecule. TPSA is an important descriptor in medicinal chemistry and drug design, as it provides an estimate of the polar surface area of a molecule.
The name assigned to the molecule according to the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) nomenclature rules, providing a standardized name for communication.
A numerical value representing the confidence or reliability of the name assigned to the molecule, indicating how well it is established in scientific literature.
The IRI of the sample location.
A user- and search engine-friendly text consisting of one or a few words as part of a URL
General remarks or additional notes regarding the molecule.
Quantative estimation of drug-likeness (q weighted sum).
Utilizing the Sugar Removal Utility to check for the presence of circular sugars.
A numerical value indicating the thoroughness or depth of the annotation provided for the molecule, reflecting its level of detail.
The logarithm of the partition between n-octanol and water (logP). AlogP is used to estimate the lipophilicity of a molecule, which is an important factor in drug absorption and distribution.
The total number of organisms associated with the molecule.
A molecule is explained through its descriptive information.
The name of the organism.
A molecule is classified by its classification.
The number of molecules included within the collection.
An additional or alternative image related to the collection.
The common or preferred name of the molecule, which may be used in various contexts and could differ from the IUPAC name.
Indicates whether the molecule serves as a parent classification in a hierarchical relationship, meaning it has child entities or variants.
The name of the sample location.
Count of molecules found in a sample location.
Number of Hydrogen Bond Donors in a molecule using the Lipinski module.
The total number of variants associated with the molecule.
The name of the location where the molecule was found.
The web address where the collection can be accessed or viewed.
A molecule has various statuses.
NPLikeness score generated using RDKit. The likelyness of a molecule to be a natural product.
Indicates whether the molecule has stereochemistry, which refers to the spatial arrangement of atoms in a molecule.
Chemical Sub Class generated using ClassyFire.
The DOI (Digital Object Identifier) of the citation.
The function calculates the volume of a molecule using RDKit's molecular modelling functionalities. It adds hydrogens to the molecule, embeds it into 3D space, and computes the molecular volume.
Direct Parent Classification generated using ClassyFire.
Utilizing the Sugar Removal Utility to check for the presence of linear sugars.
A custom function to determine the number of Lipinski's rule violations for a given molecule.
The total number of collections in which the molecule is included.
The entry and its corresponding citation.
The identifier of the collection.
The average molecular weight of the molecule.
The canonical Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) notation for the molecule, representing its structure in a line of text.
Utilizing the Sugar Removal Utility to check for the presence of circular or linear sugars.
Custom function based on CDK to get the Murko Framework.
A textual description of the current state or condition of the molecule.
The names of the authors of the citation.
Determines wheater a citation is still active or not.
Total count of the atoms.
The number rings present in a molecule.
Information about any tasks or processes performed on the collection.
Indicates whether the molecule is currently active or inactive.
Total count of the heavy atoms.
Additional remarks or notes about the collection that might provide further context or insight.
An image or visual representation associated with the collection.
The number of rotatable bonds in a molecule.
The exact molecular weight of the molecule which is based on the isotope masses of the atoms in the molecule.
The corresponding collections of the given sample location.
The number of Hydrogen Bond Acceptors in a molecule.
A molceule is labeled by an Identifier.
The title of the citation.
A hashed version of the InChI, known as the InChI Key, designed for easy digital searching and identification of the molecule.
Chemical Class generated using ClassyFire.
The hierarchical rank that helps categorize and describe the relationships from organisms to other organisms.
Indicates if there are alternative forms or variants of the entity.
The fraction of C atoms that are SP3 hybridized.
The collection includes a molecule.
An entry contains a given molecule.
Indicates whether the molecule is a tautomer, which is a specific type of chemical structure that can easily interconvert with another form.
The number of aromatic rings in a molecule.
The number of times the molecule has been cited in literature or other references.
The sample location specifies from where the molecule was extracted from.
